Collect geo-point data for a batch of requests

Source: R/collect_points.R
collect_points.Rd

Batch/panel form of collect_point(). Stacks the results of every request in requests into one long data.table, one row per (request x date x variable) for a successful collection or exactly one row for a refused request. Every per-request refusal path of collect_point() (unknown source, missing package, out-of-extent point, implausible value) applies identically.

Usage

collect_points(
  requests,
  retrieved_at = NULL,
  offline = getOption("terroir.offline", FALSE)
)

Arguments

requests

A non-empty list of geo_point_request objects (see geo_point_request()).

retrieved_at, offline

As for collect_point(); the same value is passed through to every request in the batch.

Value

A data.table with a leading request_index (position in requests) and status ("ok" or "refused") column, a reason column (NA_character_ for an "ok" row, the refusal message otherwise), followed by the fixed C6 geo_point_series columns. lon, lat and source are populated on a refused row from the request itself (the values known even when nothing was collected); the remaining C6 columns are NA on a refused row. A final call column carries the upstream call recorded in each series' provenance.

Details

Requests are grouped by source. A source registered with a batch function (see register_source()) receives all of its requests in one call, so a raster is read once for many points. Other sources are called one request at a time. Offline mode always answers one request at a time from fixtures.

A refusal is never dropped from the stack: it contributes one row with status == "refused" and reason set to the refusal's message, so a 40-site collection with two dead sources still returns 40 requests' worth of accounting, not 38.

See also

collect_point(), geo_point_request(), is_refusal()

Examples

reqs <- list(
  geo_point_request(138.6, -34.9, "2020-01-01", "2020-01-31",
                    source = "nasapower"),
  geo_point_request(0, 0, source = "no_such_source")
)
out <- suppressWarnings(collect_points(reqs, offline = TRUE))
out$status
#> [1] "refused" "refused"
